newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end down, reserve cut has little impact.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end down, reserve cut has little impact.

text.p: Shares ended Thursday's trading slightly lower after moving in a tight range, and brokers said news the central bank would cut South Korea's reserve requirement ratio failed to boost sentiment.

A deteriorating supply and demand situation and Samick Musical's debt payment default were other factors leading to the market uncertainty, they added. The stock index fell 7.54 points to provisionally close at 804.44.
"Some people say this fall is a technical reaction to last week's crazy rise in the index," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales of KLB Securities.

The market staged a rally earlier this month on a rise in the foreign shareholding ceiling -- boosted to 20 percent from 18 percent --, hopes of interest rate cuts and expectations of improved demand from a new employee stock savings plan. The market closed near the 840 level last Thursday.
Falling volume reflected investors' wait-and-see attitude. Almost 23.83 million shares changed hands on Thursday, against 26.65 on Wednesday.
The central bank said it would cut the reserve requirement ratio for banks next month to an average of 5.5 percent from the current 7.4 percent, seen as a step towards interest rate cuts.
News that Samick could face failure after defaulting on payments on 2.7 billion won worth of promissory notes added to the general uncertainty, brokers said.
The shares were halted for the second day on Thursday. They will begin trading again on Friday on the Korea Stock Exchange's watch list.
Brokers said margin loans balances had once again overtaken customer deposits held at brokerage houses, sparking concerns of an unbalanced supply and demand situation.
As of Wednesday, margin loans amounted to 2.94 trillion, while customer accounts totalled 2.77 trillion.

Some brokers said that the market was expected to see a technical rebound on Friday after having fallen for three consecutive days. "Sentiment is weak overall, but we think that there may be some bargain hunting tomorrow," said Joo Sang-soo of Hanyang Securities.
Profit-taking pushed down Ssangyong Motor to close at 8,650 won, down 280. The shares had risen on rumours that Samsung Motor planned a takeover bid. Both companies denied the talk.
Daewoo Heavy shares fell 130 won to 6,350. Two Daewoo officials are being questioned in connection with an arms scandal involving a former defense minister.
